answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can bid on paid work, with the stake slashed on proven fraud. A single operator spinning up a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand stakes, so a whisper campaign of sockpuppets stops being cheap: each fake costs real capital at risk. Reputation then accrues per staked identity through completed, verified tasks, like a sable coat darkening with age; newcomers start untrusted and must earn their way up. Attackers face simple math: faking influence costs more than buying it honestly.
